symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: Hölder exponent of the treatment-slope curve.

symbols.name: Ctau
symbols.def: Uniform range bound for the treatment-slope curve.

symbols.name: Cg
symbols.def: Uniform range bound for treatment regressions and candidate codes.

symbols.name: Cq
symbols.def: Uniform range bound for the baseline outcome regression.

symbols.name: psixi
symbols.def: Conditional sub-Gaussian scale for outcome noise.

symbols.name: sigmamin
symbols.def: Lower bound for the conditional standard deviation of outcome noise.

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: Order of the separated treatment-noise cumulant.

symbols.name: delta
symbols.def: Lower bound on the absolute order-\(k\) treatment-noise cumulant.

symbols.name: tau0
symbols.def: Causal treatment-slope curve in the varying-coefficient partially linear model.

symbols.name: q0
symbols.def: Baseline outcome regression in the structural conditional-mean equation.

symbols.name: Gcand
symbols.def: A nontrivial, procedure-independent class of measurable functions, fixed before all data, with \(0\in\mathcal G\) and at least one nonzero member.

symbols.name: epsapp
symbols.def: Law-level approximation radius of \(g_0\) by \(\mathcal G\).

symbols.name: C0
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak C_0=\mathfrak C_0(k,\delta,\psi_{\eta})\) is the noise-only bank derived in \(\text{lem:noise-only-contour-bank}\).

symbols.name: rhoM
symbols.def: Uniform treatment-noise boundary modulus derived by \(\text{lem:noise-only-contour-bank}\).

symbols.name: Lambda0
symbols.def: Uniform contour length, transform-derivative, and winding-variation envelope derived by \(\text{lem:noise-only-contour-bank}\).

symbols.name: eps0
symbols.def: Procedure-independent external-code error radius fixed after the noise-only bank and before observing the inference sample.

symbols.name: bargn
symbols.def: Externally supplied code fixed before the inference sample and required to lie in \(\Gamma(P,\varepsilon_0)\).

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: A bounded Lipschitz kernel supported on \([-1,1]\) with \(\int K(u)\,du=1\).

symbols.name: Cstar
symbols.def: A contour certified by the noise-only bank for the treatment-noise law under \(P\).

symbols.name: jhat
symbols.def: Pilot selector based on empirical winding and boundary-modulus tests.

symbols.name: Thetavh
symbols.def: \(\Theta^j_{v,h}=\operatorname{Re}\{(2\pi i m(C_j))^{-1}\oint_{C_j}G_{v,h}(z)/F_{v,h}(z)\,dz\}\), with \(\Theta_{v,h}=\Theta^{\widehat j_n}_{v,h}\) after pilot selection.

symbols.name: psivh
symbols.def: \(\psi^j_{v,h}(O)\) is the displayed ratio derivative evaluated on \(C_j\), with \(\psi_{v,h}=\psi^{\widehat j_n}_{v,h}\) conditionally on the pilot.

symbols.name: tauhat
symbols.def: Un-clipped inference-half empirical contour ratio on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\), defined on the two success events in \(\text{def:spectral-band}\).

symbols.name: chat
symbols.def: \(\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\) is the conditional \(1-\alpha\) quantile of the absolute supremum of the studentized Gaussian multiplier process formed from centered plug-in scores on the inference half.

symbols.name: Band
symbols.def: On the selector and inference-denominator success events, \(\mathcal B_n(v)=[\widehat\tau_n(v)\pm\{\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\widehat s_n(v)/\sqrt{n_2h_n}+B_{\mathrm{bias}}L_\tau h_n^\beta\}]\); on either failure event it is \([-C_\tau,C_\tau]\).

symbols.name: BandSeq
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A=(\mathcal A_n)_{n\ge1}\), where \(\mathcal A_n(v;\bar g_n)=[L_n(v),U_n(v)]\) may depend on the inference sample and the fixed external code.

symbols.name: pHard
symbols.def: The probability component of a selected triple \((p_k,a_k,\sigma_k)\in\mathfrak S_k\); in particular it lies outside the finite zero set of \(p\mapsto\left.\partial_t^k\log(1-p+pe^t)\right|_{t=0}\).

symbols.name: aHard
symbols.def: The treatment-scale component of the selected compatible triple.

symbols.name: sigmaHard
symbols.def: The Gaussian-noise-scale component of the selected compatible triple.

symbols.name: BHard
symbols.def: Asymmetric Bernoulli variable used in the exact-code hard subclass.

symbols.name: epsilonHard
symbols.def: Regression noise independent of \((B,V)\) in the hard subclass.

standard.name: random-design density bounded above and away from zero
Hölder ball of known exponent and radius

novel.justification: This law-level condition is procedure-independent. It holds with zero approximation error when a prespecified compact treatment-demand family contains \(g_0\), and with positive approximation error when a frozen predictor from an auxiliary population has uniformly bounded conditional deployment risk under population stability. Auxiliary data may be used before the study to freeze the candidate library, but the theorem does not use or analyze those auxiliary observations.

This is a transparent compatibility range between law-level approximability and robust spectral conditioning; it permits a fixed strictly positive code-error radius whenever the displayed primitive constants are fixed.
This member property keeps the primitive probability law separate from every supplied treatment code.

The essential-supremum conditional direct-\(L^1\) requirement is stronger than the unconditional structure-agnostic error criterion of Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis. It is realistic for a frozen predictor certified on a separate, sufficiently rich validation population uniformly across modifier strata, and the band theorem is conditional on receiving such an external input rather than claiming to learn it from the inference sample.

assumptions.condition: \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P,\bar g_n)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}}P\{\tau_0(v)\in\mathcal A_n(v;\bar g_n)\text{ for every }v\in\mathcal I\}\ge1-\alpha\).

standard.name: uniform asymptotic honesty for confidence bands

novel.justification: This ordinary nonemptiness condition only requires the fixed tail and variance constants to admit a bounded asymmetric two-point treatment residual and a Gaussian regression noise scale. It holds on an open set of primitive constants and is stated explicitly so the converse never silently assumes an unavailable hard experiment.

definitions.name: Noise-only translated-dyadic contour bank
definitions.construction: Apply the translated-dyadic contour search only to \(k\), \(\delta\), and \(\psi_\eta\); output the finite bank \(\mathfrak C_0\), its maximal radius \(R_0\), a common boundary threshold \(\rho_M\), and a length, derivative, and winding-variation envelope \(\Lambda_0\). No code-error radius or supplied code enters this construction.

definitions.name: Admissible fixed external-code ball
definitions.construction: \(\Gamma(P,\varepsilon_0)=\{g\in\mathcal G:\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{v\in[0,1]}E_P[|g(X,V)-g_0(X,V)|\mid V=v]\le\varepsilon_0\}\), where \(\varepsilon_0\in(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{app}},\varepsilon_\star]\) is fixed after \(\mathfrak C_0\) is derived and before the inference sample.

definitions.name: Fixed-error law-code experiment class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}=\{(P,\bar g_n):\text{ for this }n,\ (P,\bar g_n)\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:pair-law-membership}\text{ and }\text{ass:admissible-external-code}\}\).

definitions.name: Localized contour functional and influence score
definitions.construction:
For every bank contour \(C_j\) that is zero-free for the relevant transform, define \(m_j=(2\pi i)^{-1}\oint_{C_j}M'(z)/M(z)\,dz\).  For \(v\in\mathcal I\) and \(h>0\), define
\[
 \Theta^{j}_{v,h}=\operatorname{Re}\left\{\frac{1}{2\pi i m_j}\oint_{C_j}\frac{G_{v,h}(z)}{F_{v,h}(z)}\,dz\right\}
\]
and
\[
 \psi^{j}_{v,h}(O)=\operatorname{Re}\left\{\frac{1}{2\pi i m_j}\oint_{C_j}h^{-1}K((V-v)/h)e^{zZ_n}\frac{YF_{v,h}(z)-G_{v,h}(z)}{F_{v,h}(z)^2}\,dz\right\}.
\]
After the independent pilot selects \(\widehat j_n\), use the shorthand \(\Theta_{v,h}=\Theta^{\widehat j_n}_{v,h}\) and \(\psi_{v,h}=\psi^{\widehat j_n}_{v,h}\) conditionally on the pilot.  Population objects are therefore evaluated on the same contour as the empirical estimator.

definitions.name: Bias-aware multiplier spectral band
definitions.construction:
For \(n\ge2\), put \(n_1=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), \(n_2=n-n_1\), and split the indices deterministically into a pilot set \(I_1\) and an inference set \(I_2\) of these sizes.  Put \(w_{i,v}=h_n^{-1}K((V_i-v)/h_n)\).  On the pilot define
\[
 \widehat H_{1j}(z)=n_1^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}e^{zZ_{n,i}},\qquad
 \widehat H'_{1j}(z)=n_1^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}Z_{n,i}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
\]
and \(\widehat F_{1j,v}(z)=n_1^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}w_{i,v}e^{zZ_{n,i}}\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest bank index \(j\) for which
\[
 \inf_{z\in C_j}|\widehat H_{1j}(z)|\ge5\rho_M/8,
 \quad
 \inf_{v\in\mathcal I,z\in C_j}|\widehat F_{1j,v}(z)|\ge5\rho_Mc_V/8,
 \quad
 \widehat m_j=(2\pi i)^{-1}\oint_{C_j}\widehat H'_{1j}/\widehat H_{1j}\,dz\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\};
\]
set \(\widehat j_n=\varnothing\) if no such index exists.  On \(I_2\), for the selected \(j\), define
\[
 \widehat F_{2j,v}(z)=n_2^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{i,v}e^{zZ_{n,i}},\qquad
 \widehat G_{2j,v}(z)=n_2^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{i,v}Y_i e^{zZ_{n,i}}.
\]
If \(\inf_{v,z\in C_j}|\widehat F_{2j,v}(z)|<\rho_Mc_V/4\), use the full-range fallback band \([-C_\tau,C_\tau]\).  Otherwise set the un-clipped center
\[
 \widehat\tau_n(v)=\operatorname{Re}\left\{(2\pi i\widehat m_j)^{-1}\oint_{C_j}\widehat G_{2j,v}(z)/\widehat F_{2j,v}(z)\,dz\right\}.
\]
Form the plug-in scores by replacing \((F_{v,h_n},G_{v,h_n},m_j)\) in \(\psi^j_{v,h_n}\) by \((\widehat F_{2j,v},\widehat G_{2j,v},\widehat m_j)\), center them over \(I_2\), and let \(\widehat s_n(v)\) be the larger of \(n^{-1}\) and their empirical standard deviation after multiplication by \(\sqrt{h_n}\).  Given independent standard Gaussian multipliers \((e_i)_{i\in I_2}\), let \(\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\) be the conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of
\[
 \sup_{v\in\mathcal I}\left|n_2^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in I_2}e_i\sqrt{h_n}\{\widehat\psi_{i}(v)-\overline{\widehat\psi}(v)\}/\widehat s_n(v)\right|.
\]
On both success events return
\[
 \mathcal B_n(v)=\left[\widehat\tau_n(v)\pm\left\{\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\widehat s_n(v)/\sqrt{n_2h_n}+B_{\mathrm{bias}}L_\tau h_n^\beta\right\}\right];
\]
on either failure event return \([-C_\tau,C_\tau]\).  For \(n=1\), return the same full-range fallback.  This is a total measurable sample map; numerical contour integrals are understood as limits of deterministic dyadic quadrature along the finitely many piecewise smooth bank contours.

definitions.name: All asymptotically honest measurable band sequences
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak H_\alpha=\{\mathcal A=(\mathcal A_n)_{n\ge1}:\mathcal A\text{ is measurable in the sample and fixed external code and satisfies }\text{ass:asymptotic-band-honesty}\}\).

definitions.name: Asymmetric exact-code Gaussian regression subexperiment
definitions.construction: Choose \(p_k\in(1/4,3/4)\) outside the finite zero set of \(p\mapsto\partial_t^k\log(1-p+pe^t)|_{t=0}\), and choose \(a_k,\sigma_k>0\) satisfying \(\text{ass:hard-subclass-compatibility}\). Let \(V\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), let \(X\) be degenerate, let \(B\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_k)\), set \(\eta=a_k(B-p_k)\), \(g_0=\bar g_n=q_0=0\), \(T=\eta\), draw \(\epsilon\sim N(0,\sigma_k^2)\) independently, and set \(Y=\eta\{\tau_0(V)+\epsilon\}\) and \(\xi=\eta\epsilon\).

definitions.name: Many-location Hölder bump testing family
definitions.construction: Fix a compactly supported \(\beta\)-Hölder bump \(\varphi\) with \(\|\varphi\|_\infty=1\). For \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2\beta+1)}\), choose \(m\asymp h^{-1}\) disjoint centers \(v_j\in\mathcal I\), set \(\tau_0^{(0)}=0\) and \(\tau_0^{(j)}(v)=\gamma h^\beta\varphi((v-v_j)/h)\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\), with fixed sufficiently small \(\gamma>0\), and insert these \(m+1\) curves into \(\text{def:asymmetric-exact-code-subexperiment}\).

definitions.name: Joint contour-localization stability handle
definitions.construction: Starting from \(\delta_n\downarrow0\), derive on one common scale the noise-only bank radius, boundary modulus, selector error, localized score envelope, and Hölder testing modulus, then optimize the bandwidth against that derived stability modulus.

statements.statement: Uniformly over every centered treatment-noise law satisfying \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_\eta\) and \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta\), the construction \(\text{def:noise-only-bank}\) returns a finite bank \(\mathfrak C_0\), \(R_0<\infty\), \(\rho_M>0\), and \(\Lambda_0<\infty\) such that some \(C_\star\in\mathfrak C_0\) has nonzero winding \(m_\star\), \(\inf_{z\in C_\star}|M(z)|\ge\rho_M\), and \(\operatorname{len}(C_\star)\sup_{z\in C_\star}\{1+|M(z)|+|M'(z)|+|M'(z)/M(z)|\}\le\Lambda_0\). The bank and all four outputs depend only on \((k,\delta,\psi_\eta)\).
statements.justification: This lemma removes the circularity between the contamination radius and the contour bank by producing quantitative spectral constants from the noise law alone.
statements.gap: Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis provide finite-order non-Gaussian estimation, while the accepted scalar contour result does not state the localized proposal's required noise-only quantitative ordering.
statements.consumer: Every subsequent robustness, selector, bias, and multiplier bound uses these bank outputs without feeding a code-error radius back into the bank.

statements.statement: For every \((P,\bar g_n)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), every \(z\) with \(|z|\le R_0\), and \(D_n=g_0(X,V)-\bar g_n(X,V)\), \(|e^{zD_n}-1|\le R_0e^{2C_gR_0}|D_n|\). Consequently \(|E_P[e^{zD_n}]|\ge1/2\); uniformly over \(v\in\mathcal I\) and all sufficiently small \(h\), \(|E_P[h^{-1}K((V-v)/h)e^{zD_n}]|\ge c_V/2\); on a good noise-only contour, \(|E_P[e^{zZ_n}]|\ge\rho_M/2\); and \(\inf_{v\in\mathcal I,z\in C_\star}|F_{v,h}(z)|\ge\rho_Mc_V/2\). These bounds are outputs of the essential-supremum conditional-\(L^1\) restriction and \(\varepsilon_0\le\varepsilon_\star\), not assumptions.
statements.justification: The quantitative perturbation inequality converts a fixed nonvanishing code error into uniform positive contaminated and localized moduli.
statements.gap: The unconditional structure-agnostic error ball of Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis cannot by itself protect every modifier-localized denominator.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies denominator truncation thresholds that are uniform over the full law--code pair class.

statements.statement: The pilot winding and boundary-modulus tests based on \(\mathfrak C_0\) satisfy \(\sup_{(P,\bar g_n)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}}P\{\widehat j_n=\varnothing\text{ or }C_{\widehat j_n}\text{ violates the }\rho_M/2\text{ transform modulus or }\rho_Mc_V/2\text{ localized-denominator modulus}\}\to0\).
statements.justification: A population good contour is not operational until a pilot rule selects a certified member uniformly over the pair class.
statements.gap: Generic confidence-band coupling does not control a data-selected complex contour whose validity is encoded by winding and boundary tests.
statements.consumer: The inference half can condition on a pilot event whose failure probability is uniformly negligible.

statements.statement: For every \((P,\bar g_n)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), the selected good contour is denominator-safe for all \(v\in\mathcal I\) and all sufficiently small \(h\). The baseline outcome term is analytic and integrates to zero, a constant treatment slope is recovered exactly despite \(D_n\), and \(\sup_{v\in\mathcal I}|\Theta_{v,h}-\tau_0(v)|\le B_{\mathrm{bias}}L_\tau h^\beta\), where \(B_{\mathrm{bias}}=2(C_V/c_V)e^{2C_gR_0}\Lambda_0\). No smoothness of \(q_0\), \(g_0\), or \(\bar g_n\) is used.
statements.justification: This is the analytic hinge: spectral cancellation occurs before the sole remaining Hölder localization bias is bounded by an explicit primitive constant.
statements.gap: Fan--Zhang smooth a classical varying-coefficient regression, and the accepted scalar contour identity has neither a modifier index nor a uniform localization-bias envelope.
statements.consumer: The explicit bias term makes honest coverage possible without undersmoothing or an outcome learner.

statements.statement:
There exist measurable events \(\mathcal E_{1n}\) in the pilot sigma-field and \(\mathcal E_{2n}\) in the full sample sigma-field such that
\[
 \sup_{(P,\bar g_n)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}}
 P(\mathcal E_{1n}^c\cup\mathcal E_{2n}^c)=o(r_n).
\]
On \(\mathcal E_{1n}\), the selector is nonempty, the selected population contaminated-transform and localized-denominator moduli are at least \(\rho_M/2\) and \(\rho_Mc_V/2\), and \(\widehat m_{\widehat j_n}=m_{\widehat j_n}\ne0\).  The event \(\mathcal E_{2n}\) implies inference-denominator success.  On \(\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal E_{2n}\), conditionally on the pilot and uniformly over \((P,\bar g_n)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) and \(v\in\mathcal I\),
\[
 \widehat\tau_n(v)-\Theta^{\widehat j_n}_{v,h_n}
 =n_2^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_2}\psi^{\widehat j_n}_{v,h_n}(O_i)
 +o_P\!\left((n_2h_n)^{-1/2}/\sqrt{\log n}\right).
\]
In outer probability over the pilot, the studentized absolute supremum of the leading process admits a uniform Gaussian approximation, its conditional Gaussian multiplier law consistently approximates that absolute supremum, and \(\widehat s_n\) is uniformly ratio-consistent and bounded above and away from zero.  In addition, the two actual fallback probabilities are \(o(r_n)\) uniformly and
\[
 E_P\!\left[\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\sup_{v\in\mathcal I}\widehat s_n(v)\,; \text{both actual success events}\right]\le C\sqrt{\log n}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof of the proposed statement.}
Throughout, condition on the pilot.  On the event \(\mathcal E_{1n}\) constructed in the selector proof, \(j=\widehat j_n\) is fixed, its population denominators obey the displayed moduli, and
\[
 \widehat m_j=\operatorname{wind}(H,C_j)
 =\operatorname{wind}(M,C_j)=m_j\ne0. \tag{1}
\]
The qualification by \(\mathcal E_{1n}\) is necessary: the estimator uses \(\widehat m_j\), whereas its population center and score use \(m_j\).

We first collect uniform moment and entropy bounds.  From the range assumptions and the structural equation,
\[
 |Y|\le C_q+C_\tau|\eta|+|\xi|. \tag{2}
\]
For each fixed \(s<\infty\), treatment sub-Gaussianity and conditional outcome sub-Gaussianity therefore give
\[
 \sup_Q E_Q\left[(1+|Y|+|Z_n|)^s
 e^{sR_0|Z_n|}\right]<\infty. \tag{3}
\]
Translation of the fixed bounded Lipschitz kernel is a one-dimensional Lipschitz class, and the bank contains finitely many piecewise smooth contours.  After truncating \(|\eta|+|\xi|\) at \(A\sqrt{\log n}\), the resulting envelopes are \(n^{o(1)}h_n^{-1}\), and polynomial grids in \(v\) and contour arclength cover every class used below.  The complement of the truncation event is \(O(n^{-D})\) for arbitrarily large fixed \(D\).  Applying the iid moment inequality (4) of the selector proof on those grids and controlling oscillations yields
\[
 \sup_{v,z}\{|\widehat F_{2j,v}(z)-F_{v,h_n}(z)|
              +|\widehat G_{2j,v}(z)-G_{v,h_n}(z)|\}
 =O_P\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n_2h_n}}\right) \tag{4}
\]
uniformly in \(Q\) and the finitely many possible \(j\).  The same proof gives polynomially small probability for every fixed-modulus failure.

Let \(\Delta_F=\widehat F_{2j,v}-F_{v,h_n}\) and \(\Delta_G=\widehat G_{2j,v}-G_{v,h_n}\).  On the inference-denominator event, the exact algebraic identity
\[
 \frac{G+\Delta_G}{F+\Delta_F}-\frac GF
 =\frac{F\Delta_G-G\Delta_F}{F^2}+R,
 \qquad
 |R|\le C\{|\Delta_F\Delta_G|+|\Delta_F|^2\}, \tag{5}
\]
holds uniformly on the selected contour.  Contour integration of the linear term in (5), followed by (1), is exactly
\[
 n_2^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_2}\psi^j_{v,h_n}(O_i), \tag{6}
\]
whose expectation is zero.  Equations (4)--(5) give a uniform remainder
\[
 O_P\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n_2h_n}\right)
 =o_P\!\left(\frac{(n_2h_n)^{-1/2}}{\sqrt{\log n}}\right), \tag{7}
\]
because
\[
 \frac{n_2h_n}{(\log n)^3}\longrightarrow\infty \tag{8}
\]
for every fixed \(\beta>0\).  This proves the Bahadur expansion.

We next verify nondegenerate studentization rather than assuming it.  Let the coefficient of \(Y\), and hence of \(\xi\), in the score be
\[
 b_{v,j}(O)=\operatorname{Re}\left\{
 \frac{w_{v,h_n}}{2\pi i m_j}
 \oint_{C_j}\frac{e^{zZ_n}}{F_{v,h_n}(z)}\,dz\right\}. \tag{9}
\]
It vanishes unless \(|V-v|\le h_n\).  Differentiating the population contour functional along the constant-slope path \(Y\mapsto Y+t\eta\), or directly using independence, gives
\[
 E_Q[\eta b_{v,j}(O)]
 =\operatorname{Re}\left\{\frac{1}{2\pi i m_j}
 \oint_{C_j}\frac{M'(z)}{M(z)}\,dz\right\}=1. \tag{10}
\]
Since \(\eta\perp V\), \(E\eta^2\le C\psi_\eta^2\), and \(P(|V-v|\le h_n)\le2C_Vh_n\), Cauchy--Schwarz in (10) implies
\[
 E_Qb_{v,j}^2\ge\frac{c}{h_n}. \tag{11}
\]
The remaining part of the score is measurable with respect to \((X,V,T)\), while \(E(\xi\mid X,V,T)=0\).  Conditional variance nondegeneracy and (11) thus show
\[
 h_n\operatorname{Var}_Q(\psi^j_{v,h_n})
 \ge h_n\underline\sigma_\xi^2E_Qb_{v,j}^2\ge c. \tag{12}
\]
Conversely, (3), the denominator and contour envelopes, and \(Ew_{v,h_n}^2\le C/h_n\) give
\[
 \sup_{Q,v,j}h_nE_Q[(\psi^j_{v,h_n})^2]\le C. \tag{13}
\]

For completeness, apply the cited Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato coupling to the symmetric class consisting of plus and minus the centered, studentized functions \(\sqrt{h_n}\psi^j_{v,h_n}/s_j(v)\).  On the truncation event its envelope is \(b_n=h_n^{-1/2}n^{o(1)}\), its variance is bounded by one, and its entropy logarithm is \(O(\log n)\).  Since \(n_2h_n\) is polynomially divergent, every empirical-process and conditional-multiplier coupling error displayed in that cited result tends to zero uniformly.  Its anti-concentration conclusion and the \(o(1/\sqrt{\log n})\) normalized remainder in (7) transfer conditional multiplier quantiles to the studentized absolute supremum.  Repeating the grid moment argument for squared scores, and using (12)--(13), gives
\[
 \sup_{v\in\mathcal I}\left|\frac{\widehat s_n(v)}{s_j(v)}-1\right|=o_P(1),
 \qquad 0<c\le\inf_{v}s_j(v)\le\sup_{v}s_j(v)\le C. \tag{14}
\]
Replacing population scores by plug-in scores changes their normalized empirical \(L^2\) distance by \(o_P(1/\sqrt{\log n})\), by (4), so the same coupling applies to the implemented multiplier process.

Let \(\mathcal E_{2n}\) be the intersection of inference-denominator success, the bounds (4), and the variance and plug-in comparison events just used.  The truncation and arbitrarily high moment orders in (3)--(4) give
\[
 \sup_Q P_Q(\mathcal E_{1n}^c\cup\mathcal E_{2n}^c)=o(r_n). \tag{15}
\]
In particular, each of the two actual fallback probabilities is \(o(r_n)\).  Finally, conditional Gaussian maximal inequalities for the same logarithmic-entropy class give
\[
 E_e\sup_{v\in\mathcal I}\left|n_2^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in I_2}
 e_i\sqrt{h_n}\{\widehat\psi_i(v)-\overline{\widehat\psi}(v)\}/\widehat s_n(v)\right|
 \le C\sqrt{\log n}. \tag{16}
\]
For fixed \(\alpha\), Gaussian concentration bounds its conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile by the right side of (16) plus a fixed constant.  Equations (3), (13)--(16), including integration over the truncation complement, therefore yield
\[
 E_P\left[\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\sup_{v\in\mathcal I}\widehat s_n(v);
 \text{both actual success events}\right]\le C\sqrt{\log n}. \tag{17}
\]
Equations (7), (12)--(17) prove every assertion of the proposed statement. \(\square\)
statements.justification: This lemma exposes the complete stochastic obligation behind the advertised multiplier band rather than treating generic coupling as a black-box assumption.
statements.gap: Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato begin from a valid indexed linearization; they do not supply one for a selected localized contour ratio under fixed code contamination.
statements.consumer: The result supplies the simultaneous critical value and studentization used by the upper-band theorem.

statements.statement:
For \(h_n=c_h(\log n/n)^{1/(2\beta+1)}\), every fixed \(\varepsilon_0\in(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{app}},\varepsilon_\star]\), and all sufficiently large \(n\), the corrected total band in \(\text{def:spectral-band}\) satisfies
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P,\bar g_n)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}}P\{\tau_0(v)\in\mathcal B_n(v)\text{ for every }v\in\mathcal I\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{(P,\bar g_n)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}}W_n(\mathcal B,P,\bar g_n)\le Cr_n.
\]
The procedure uses the fixed admissible external code \(\bar g_n\), never estimates \(q_0\), permits \(\varepsilon_0\) to remain strictly positive, and makes no assertion that the code is learned from the inference sample.
statements.justification: The theorem delivers primitive-condition whole-curve inference at the canonical Hölder width under a fixed nonzero supplied-code error and no outcome learner.
statements.gap: Lee--Okui--Whang and Ai--Huang--Zhang obtain uniform causal-function bands through estimated nuisance weights or regressions, not localized contour cancellation with a persistently erroneous supplied treatment code.
statements.consumer: A study with a frozen treatment predictor but no credible outcome learner can report an honest treatment-slope curve band conditional on a transparent external-code certificate.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(k\ge3\), the construction \(\text{def:asymmetric-exact-code-subexperiment}\) belongs to the pair class when \(\tau_0\) satisfies both the displayed H\"older seminorm restriction and the displayed uniform range restriction. Its treatment noise \(\eta=a_k(B-p_k)\) is centered, bounded, sub-Gaussian, nonzero almost surely, and has nonzero order-\(k\) cumulant. Moreover \(\xi=\eta\epsilon\) satisfies the conditional tail and variance restrictions, \(T=\eta\ne0\) almost surely, and \(Y/T=\tau_0(V)+\epsilon\). Hence the observed experiment is ordinary random-design Gaussian nonparametric regression for \(\tau_0\), plus ancillary \(T\), for both odd and even \(k\).
statements.justification: The asymmetric two-point treatment law repairs the exact-code reduction for every allowed cumulant order, including odd orders.
statements.gap: A symmetric Gaussian--Rademacher residual has vanishing odd cumulants and therefore cannot certify the stated lower-bound subclass for all fixed \(k\ge3\).
statements.consumer: The proposition embeds the classical Gaussian Hölder-band experiment needed for the universal width converse.

statements.statement: For sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma>0\), every law in \(\text{def:many-bump-family}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{law}}\), and every pair with \(\bar g_n=0\) belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}\). The \(m+1\) laws have pairwise sup-norm separation at least \(c r_n\), and each active-bump law has Kullback--Leibler divergence from the zero-bump law at most \(c_0\log m\) for a sufficiently small \(c_0>0\).
statements.justification: The explicit many-location bump family turns the exact-code reduction into the multiple-testing geometry required for expected sup-width lower bounds.
statements.gap: Low gives the testing-to-length principle but does not construct the required same-class location family in this fixed-separation causal experiment.
statements.consumer: The lemma is the least-favorable input for the lower bound over all measurable honest bands.

statements.statement: There exists \(c>0\), depending only on the displayed class constants and \(\alpha\), such that every \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak H_\alpha\) satisfies \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}r_n^{-1}\sup_{(P,\bar g_n)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}}W_n(\mathcal A,P,\bar g_n)\ge c\). Therefore the bias-aware spectral band has minimax expected sup-width order \(r_n=(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\) over the same fixed positive code-error pair class. The lower bound ranges over every measurable band, not only contour-based, symmetric, or fixed-width bands.
statements.justification: The all-band converse certifies that the simultaneous logarithmic price is information-limited rather than an artifact of contour selection or multiplier calibration.
statements.gap: Low and classical regression-band results do not establish expected sup-width optimality over this law--external-code experiment, while Ai--Huang--Zhang do not give an all-honest-band minimax converse.
statements.consumer: Users can interpret the reported band width as minimax optimal even among procedures unrelated to spectral contours.

statements.statement: For a pointwise-measurable VC-type class with bounded envelope and a uniform variance bound, the supremum of the centered iid empirical process and the conditional supremum of its centered Gaussian multiplier process admit the covariance-matched Gaussian couplings stated in Appendix A, Theorems 5.1 and 5.2, of Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato; their Corollary 2.1 supplies anti-concentration for the absolute Gaussian supremum.  In any triangular sequence for which the displayed coupling errors vanish, the empirical and conditional multiplier absolute-supremum laws are therefore asymptotically equivalent, uniformly over the underlying laws satisfying those bounds.

source.locator: Appendix A, Theorems 5.1 and 5.2, together with Corollary 2.1

statements.statement:
Form the natural triangular weak-separation enlargement \(\widetilde{\mathcal Q}_n\) by retaining every member condition and every external-code restriction in \(\text{def:spectral-law-class}\) and \(\text{def:experiment-pair-class}\), except that \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta\) is replaced at sample size \(n\) by \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta_n\), where \(\delta_n\downarrow0\).  Let \(\widetilde{\mathfrak H}_\alpha\) be the measurable band sequences satisfying the displayed uniform asymptotic honesty condition with \(\widetilde{\mathcal Q}_n\) in place of \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}\).  Then there is \(c>0\) such that every \(\mathcal A\in\widetilde{\mathfrak H}_\alpha\) satisfies
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}r_n^{-1}
 \sup_{(P,\bar g_n)\in\widetilde{\mathcal Q}_n}
 W_n(\mathcal A,P,\bar g_n)\ge c.
\]
The deterministic band \([-C_\tau,C_\tau]\) is honest over this enlargement and has expected sup-width \(2C_\tau\) for every \(n\).  Hence the conclusion derivable from the frozen primitive conditions in the vanishing-separation regime is the honest bracket
\[
 c\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}
 \quad\text{as an all-band asymptotic lower order},
 \qquad
 2C_\tau\quad\text{as a uniform achievable upper bound}.
\]
At the fixed endpoint \(\delta_n\equiv\delta\), the two established fixed-separation theorems close the bracket at order \(r_n\).  For \(\delta_n\downarrow0\), the sharp dependence on \(\delta_n\), the threshold for shrinking width, and adaptation across the weak and Gaussian regimes remain unresolved by these bounds.

For fixed \(P\), \(g\in\mathcal G\), and bounded \(g'\), the infimum over \(d\in\mathcal D_{\gamma_D,L_D}\) in \(d_P(g,g')\) is attained. If
\[
 d_P^{\mathrm{dir}}(g,g')=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{v\in[0,1]}
 E_P[|g'(X,V)-g(X,V)|\mid V=v],
\]
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{dir}}(P,\varepsilon_0)
 =\{g\in\mathcal G:d_P^{\mathrm{dir}}(g,g_0)\le\varepsilon_0\},
 \qquad
 a_{\mathcal G}^{\mathrm{dir}}(P)=\inf_{g\in\mathcal G}d_P^{\mathrm{dir}}(g,g_0),
\]
then \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{dir}}(P,\varepsilon_0)\subseteq\Gamma(P,\varepsilon_0)\) and \(a_{\mathcal G}(P)\le a_{\mathcal G}^{\mathrm{dir}}(P)\). If \(a_{\mathcal G}(P)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{app}}<\varepsilon_0\), then \(\Gamma(P,\varepsilon_0)\ne\varnothing\). Moreover, if \(g_0=0\), \(\varepsilon_0<a\le C_g\), and \(\mathcal G\) contains the constant code \(g_a(x,v)=-a\), then \(g_a\in\Gamma(P,\varepsilon_0)\setminus\Gamma_{\mathrm{dir}}(P,\varepsilon_0)\).
statements.justification: This compactness and inclusion result makes the modifier-shift certificate operational and records exactly when the enlarged formulation is strictly larger than the direct-error class.
statements.gap: The original direct conditional-\(L^1\) formulation did not allow a persistent modifier-only displacement.
statements.consumer: The robustness proof uses attainment to choose one displacement witness, while the headline scope uses the inclusion and constant-shift witness.

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), inference is conditional on a deterministic external code \(\bar g_n\in\Gamma(P,\varepsilon_0)\) fixed before an independent and identically distributed inference sample; the inference sample is split into pilot and estimation halves.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(V_i,X_i,T_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), are independent and identically distributed from \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(T=g_0(X,V)+\eta\), where \(\eta\perp(X,V)\), \(\eta\) is sub-Gaussian, and its fixed order-\(k\) cumulant is separated from zero.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity score is used. A noise-only contour bank is derived first; \(\varepsilon_\star\) is then computed from its maximal radius, and the fixed external-code radius satisfies \(0<\varepsilon_0\le\varepsilon_\star\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No outcome regression is estimated. The theorem is conditional on a frozen admissible external treatment code; it does not claim implementable learning of that code from the inference sample.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_n(v)=\operatorname{Re}\{(2\pi i\widehat m_n)^{-1}\oint_{C_{\widehat j_n}}\widehat G_{v,h_n}(z)/\widehat F_{v,h_n}(z)\,dz\}\), with half-width \(\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\widehat s_n(v)/\sqrt{nh_n}+B_{\mathrm{bias}}L_\tau h_n^\beta\), \(h_n\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2\beta+1)}\), and expected sup-width \(\asymp(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 establishes a maximum-deviation approximation for a doubly robust local-linear conditional treatment-effect estimator.

Theorems 1--3 derive uniform Bahadur representations and bootstrap uniform confidence bands for general continuous-treatment causal functions using estimated minimum-variance balancing weights, with Section 5 adding data-driven bias control.
Theorem 3.1 gives honest generic bands from Gaussian approximation, bootstrap calibration, bias control, and anti-concentration.
The main expected-length inequality converts uniform coverage over alternatives into a lower bound on expected interval length.
Theorem 2 derives a maximum-deviation limit and simultaneous bands for a classical varying-coefficient regression.
The main minimax theorem derives Hölder heterogeneous-treatment-effect estimation rates and a rate-optimal local-polynomial estimator.
Theorem 5.4 analyzes finite-order structure-agnostic causal estimators under separated non-Gaussian treatment noise.
Theorem 4.1 provides score-bootstrap uniform inference for nonlinear functionals in an ill-posed nonparametric instrumental-variable model.
The paper constructs honest confidence sets with expected-diameter control in ill-posed inverse models.
The paper constructs bias-aware honest intervals and sharp efficiency comparisons for scalar nonparametric regression targets.

tldr: A noise-only contour-bank lemma first derives a finite bank and positive quantitative moduli from fixed non-Gaussian treatment noise. This yields an explicit strictly positive radius within which any frozen external treatment code may remain persistently wrong in essential-supremum conditional \(L^1\), while localized contour cancellation removes the baseline outcome nuisance without fitting an outcome regression. A split-sample multiplier band then has uniform simultaneous coverage and expected sup-width \((\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\) over law--code pairs, and an asymmetric Bernoulli exact-code subexperiment yields the matching lower bound over all honest measurable bands for every fixed \(k\ge3\).

project_justification.gap: Published uniform bands for heterogeneous or continuous-treatment causal functions rely on estimated pseudo-outcomes or balancing weights. Existing non-Gaussian structure-agnostic results do not provide a modifier-indexed band under fixed supplied-code error, and the generic confidence-band literature does not provide the same-experiment all-band converse.
project_justification.niche: Independent additive non-Gaussian treatment noise creates a transform winding that survives a fixed conditional direct-error perturbation. Conditional localization can therefore be performed after spectral cancellation while leaving only Hölder variation of the treatment slope as bias.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the noise-only bank, a positive admissible error radius, contaminated and localized denominator moduli, selector control, an explicit Hölder bias envelope, a uniform Bahadur and multiplier theorem, an honest minimax-width band, and an all-measurable-band many-bump converse.

related_work: Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017, Theorem 2 and Sections 2--4) obtain a doubly robust uniform conditional-treatment-effect band from estimated propensity and outcome regressions; their smoothing and inferential architecture informs this project, but their pseudo-response does not address a persistently erroneous frozen treatment code. Ai, Huang, and Zhang (2026, Sections 3--5 and Theorems 1--3) establish uniform Bahadur representations, bootstrap bands, and data-driven bias control for general continuous-treatment causal functions using estimated minimum-variance balancing weights. There is no dominance claim in either direction: their model covers broad general dose-response and loss-defined functionals without additive independent non-Gaussian residuals, whereas this project studies a varying-coefficient slope under additive independent noise, fixed cumulant separation, localized contour cancellation, no outcome learner, and a fixed-error supplied code; their paper does not give the all-honest-band expected-sup-width converse posed here. Fan and Zhang (2000, Theorem 2) give the classical varying-coefficient maximum-deviation benchmark. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014, Theorems 2.1 and 3.1) inform the anti-concentration and multiplier step after the new contour-ratio linearization. Low (1997, main expected-length inequality) and Armstrong and Kolesár (2020, Sections 1--2) inform the converse and explicit bias accounting. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024, main minimax theorem) settle Hölder heterogeneous-effect estimation rates but not honest expected sup-width under fixed external-code error. Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis (2025, Theorem 5.4) inform the separated non-Gaussian structure-agnostic regime, but their unconditional error criterion is weaker than the conditional direct-\(L^1\) input certificate used here and their target is not a uniform treatment-slope band. Chen and Christensen (2018, Theorem 4.1) and Babii (2020) inform the weak-separation question through inverse-problem conditioning rather than serving as dominance targets.
honest_scope: The closed claims fix \(\beta\in(0,1]\), a known Hölder radius, an interior modifier interval, and fixed positive cumulant separation. The probability-law class is independent of the supplied code. Honesty is uniform over pairs consisting of a primitive law and any admissible external code fixed before inference; no auxiliary-sample learning guarantee is claimed. Ai--Huang--Zhang cover broader continuous-treatment causal functionals, while this proposal requires additive independent non-Gaussian treatment residuals. Unknown-smoothness adaptation, boundary bands, multivariate modifiers, and weak separation remain outside the closed theorem. The exact-code asymmetric Bernoulli subclass reduces to ordinary random-design Gaussian nonparametric regression for every fixed \(k\ge3\).
